targets.authors: Bargh JA, Chen M, Burrows L
targets.title: Automaticity of social behavior: direct effects of trait construct and stereotype-activation on action.
targets.evidence_quote:
Here, we sought to replicate Bargh et al's
[1]
experiments.
targets.outcome_quote: Despite the use of automated timing methods and a larger sample, our first experiment failed to show priming. Our second experiment was aimed at manipulating the beliefs of the experimenters: Half were led to think that participants would walk slower when primed congruently, and the other half was led to expect the opposite. Strikingly, we obtained a walking speed effect, but only when experimenters believed participants would indeed walk slower.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly report failure in Experiment 1 and conditional replication in Experiment 2, including objective timings. The paper questions automaticity, awareness and expectancy but does not give an overall verdict that overrides its opposing study results; aggregate mixed rather than treating one condition as the whole attempt.

reasoning: Two new-sample experiments retest Bargh et al. experiments 2a and 2b. Earlier replication attempts cited as context are not separately retested. The conflicting replication outcomes are aggregated for the single original paper.
